title: Your barcode doesn't contain the price. Here's what it does
description: A barcode is just an ID number, printed as bars. The price lives in the store's database.

scenes.big: A barcode doesn't hold the price
scenes.say: The barcode on your snack doesn't contain its price. So what do those stripes actually say?
The first barcode scanned at a checkout was on a ten-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, in Troy, Ohio, on June twenty-sixth, nineteen seventy-four.

steps: Scanner shines light on the bars
Dark and light bars reflect differently
Check digit confirms a clean read
scenes.say: The bars are a code for a number. A scanner shines light across them and reads the pattern of dark and light. The last digit is a check digit, calculated from the others, so the scanner knows if it misread.
Here's an example number. The scanner sends it to the store's system, which replies with the item and price.

That number just identifies the product. The store's computer looks it up and finds the price. So prices can change without a single sticker being reprinted. The barcode is only a name tag. The store holds everything else. Follow for more everyday tech.
